seed_checks.scope: Derived from seed.ts:61-76; sampled against baseline seeded API suite. S14 and C1 narrative totals are correct. Other concrete numerical errors are listed below.

findings.finding: When workspace path changes, useJson retains the previous successful data until the new request succeeds, including after a failed request. Workboard immediately renders the old itemList under the newly selected workspace. A slow or failed Borealis fetch can leave Apollo cards/actions visible under Borealis; the existing switch test waits for eventual replacement and does not cover this interval or failure.
findings.repair: Clear or key data by request path on selection changes, including error states, and add a delayed/failed-switch public regression. Preserve the intentionally unguarded draft discard behavior.

findings.finding: The contract says all errors use the app envelope and every unauthenticated endpoint except health/auth returns 401, yet an unknown unauthenticated endpoint returns 404 and Better Auth's wrong-credentials HTTP response is {message,code}, not the app envelope. These are real observed outputs, not a request to normalize Better Auth internals.
findings.repair: Reconcile the public wording with actual unknown-route precedence and explicitly exempt or accurately describe Better Auth errors; align FAQ and tests. Alternatively change the implementation uniformly if the author intentionally prefers the other policy.

findings.finding: Fresh npm ci lacks a Playwright browser: documented self-contained check:full initially exited 1 with missing chromium executable. Chromium installation followed by the same check passed. In non-CI mode reuseExistingServer may also silently use another listener on 4599 instead of the reset, isolated DB.
findings.repair: Document the pinned Playwright browser installation and OS prerequisites, and make fresh isolated server/reset behavior explicit or disable server reuse for qualification.

findings.finding: C1's acceptance table claims 5/3 for seed where the requirement correctly says 4/3; changed option labels also break ownership.spec.ts selectOption labels and the fresh workspace assertion, not just auth option assertions cited. C2 title_asc first is Archive old assets, not Audit analytics events. General FAQ and contract README prohibit all baseline test edits while C1 explicitly requires them.
findings.repair: Correct examples and enumerate minimally permitted changes to all affected public test assertions with a uniform precedence rule; retain behavioral regression coverage.

findings.finding: C3 does not specify partial/malformed links, signed-out application timing, and clipboard failure; C4 calls a single overwritten pair a per-user store, although it cannot remember multiple users simultaneously. Its per-user acceptance check uses a fresh context where the key is absent, so it does not test mismatch isolation.
findings.repair: State link/error and sign-in timing boundaries and clipboard failure policy; describe C4 as a last-user single slot or specify a true per-user store, and test mismatch in the same browser storage context.

findings.finding: S01 disables empty submit while baseline e2e requires clicking it and observing server error; changing the shared title validator also conflicts with a baseline unit assertion for whitespace-only input. S08 replaces raw date UI with time-dependent labels while baseline e2e requires raw Due dates; its leap-day POST omits required title, and the far-future Dec 2026 example becomes volatile with real time.
findings.repair: Explicitly authorize only necessary assertion migrations for changed semantics (or retain equivalent baseline helpers where appropriate); provide valid POST bodies and pin server time for date examples/tests; resolve FAQ/README blanket prohibition.

findings.finding: S02 simultaneously says archived items are excluded from and included in filter=archived. S03 guarantees no repeats across updates while encoding only the current updatedAt/id cursor and specifies no snapshot, seen-ID set, immutable order, or clock assumptions. A previously served item moved to a key after the cursor can be served again; ordinary PATCH sets updated_at to the server clock, so this requires a backward clock or another way to move an item's key backwards, not an ordinary monotonic-clock PATCH. The guarantee does not state that limitation. A list-level data-page cannot separately mark multiple appended pages without further interpretation.
findings.repair: Correct S02 wording. Choose a realizable explicit pagination consistency model and cursor/state design, with concrete mutation scenarios and page markup semantics before authoring evaluators.

findings.finding: S05's example lists an incorrect created_at order, and its exact item field list omits workspaceId while requiring every work_items column exactly once. Comparing JSON.parse(export) directly to a snake_case SQLite row also cannot literally hold. C2 independently has a wrong title-first example.
findings.repair: Publish the correct ordered IDs; include workspaceId in the exact ordered export shape or explicitly exempt the column; state equality after specified camelCase mapping.

findings.finding: S06 says a PATCH of title is forbidden to non-creator members, while its disabled-title UI must still save other fields and baseline sends every field including title; unchanged-title presence versus actual rename is undefined. S09 puts a full object in fields.currentItem although baseline specifies fields as string messages only and the client/server types require string values; Reload latest also lacks a single-item GET endpoint in baseline.
findings.repair: Specify whether unchanged title is allowed or omitted and show a noncreator UI save; explicitly define a typed conflict payload exception and its lookup/refetch path, preserving the existing envelope for baseline errors.

findings.finding: S10 examples ask ada to select Borealis although she is not a member; create dirty='any non-empty field' conflicts with default nonempty status=open, and <form title> is undefined. S11 says three selected, then select all, but announces 2 in eight-item Apollo; duplicate item IDs have unspecified update/version/count semantics. S04 says random server IDs yet calls them pinned, and does not define first-error priority or exact oversized-array error despite examples claiming a limit message.
findings.repair: Use bruno for switches; define dirty against defaults and form-title formatting; fix bulk example and explicitly decide duplicate-ID behavior; clarify import error priority/messages and generated-ID example.

findings.finding: S07 says 'with consent' but auto-prefills, and 'non-empty, changed' is ambiguous for an edit cleared to empty and in-flight debounce cancellation. S08's helper takes a day string but the UTC-flip example passes timestamps, and singular/plural day labels are unspecified. S12 heading mentions status/title only while body includes notes/dueDate; invalid limit handling and event/change atomicity are not explicit. S15 incorrectly says mouse is required in the baseline despite keyboard-operable buttons.
findings.repair: Define actual draft trigger and consent model, UTC time interface/label grammar, history field set/limit errors and transactional consistency; correct keyboard baseline description without treating the missing shortcut as already implemented.

findings.finding: Most contracts are coherent independent increments against a reset baseline, but C1/S14 both count open items, S01/S08/S09 share validation/PATCH, S07/S10 edit-state, S02/S03 list, S06/S13 authorization, and S04/S05 related but incompatible formats. Their shared primitives are meaningful overlap rather than proof of duplicate tasks. FAQ leaves per-task reset as a coordinator decision.
findings.repair: Decide and publish reset-to-baseline per task before freeze, keep overlap advisories, and avoid combined-task acceptance assumptions. No model-favoring selection is recommended.

findings.finding: The package inventory covers direct core stack versions and correctly flags better-sqlite3 type/runtime mismatch; all 21 direct package pins match the lock and runtime SQLite reports 3.53.4. Links mostly target current/latest docs rather than version-pinned snapshots. Node runtime and SQLite language references and browser clipboard/storage/history/accessibility references relevant to tasks are missing; baseline README points to docs/source-inventory.json within baseline but it actually lives in ../docs. No Context archives are claimed.
findings.repair: Add official relevant Node/SQLite and browser API sources, version/commit or retrieval context and coverage/omission statements, and correct the README path; do not imply Context archives or upstream documentation were independently qualified.

findings.finding: record_id hashes unescaped colon-separated fields: (run='a:b',session='c') collides with (run='a',session='b:c') for the same response and source; deduplicate then silently drops a distinct request. Within the same identity the last snapshot unconditionally replaces an earlier complete snapshot, so a later incomplete snapshot can erase billable output. Conflicting mappings or actor attribution under that ID are also silently lost; identical provider response IDs attributed to different sessions remain separate by design and need global reconciliation to avoid double charging.
findings.repair: Use unambiguous canonical tuple serialization, validate source/session/actor conflicts, define final-snapshot ordering/completeness and retain raw snapshots or flag missing/conflicting counters. Specify cross-session response identity reconciliation, not summing independent views.

findings.finding: The normalizer maps the observed GLM 19/89/104 example correctly: billable completion 89, reasoning diagnostic 104, not 193; missing values remain null. However it accepts any mapping_id/provider/model without checking that the mapping is qualified, treats conflicting non-null cache aliases as if the first were authoritative (including 0 versus 7), emits negative cost or invalid actor/phase despite its schema, and malformed nested detail types raise AttributeError rather than a defined validation result.
findings.repair: Gate mappings by verified provider/model/version; flag unequal alias conflicts while choosing aliases once only when documented; validate metadata, nested objects and finite nonnegative cost before emission, or validate the produced record against the schema. Preserve unknowns and raw provider data.

findings.finding: source is a fixed asserted label, actor/session are unchecked caller values, parent_session_id/resolved_model/actual_provider/native_usage are always null, and no immutable raw-event reference, request timing, endpoint identity or session ancestry is captured. Schema permits reconciliation=crosschecked without requiring corroborating evidence. These are draft provenance limitations, not evidence that a full broker has been qualified or failed.
findings.repair: At integration, validate actor/session/source against controller events, represent evidence-backed reconciliation and provenance, retain raw events, and separately qualify provider-specific aliases, captures, retries, native joins and billing. Do not infer revision, zeros or extra charges.
